newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude off on products, seen rangebound.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude off on products, seen rangebound.

text.p: NYMEX crude remained lower Monday afternoon after warmer-than-expected temperature forecasts sparked a decline in refined products, but traders saw crude rangebound until the close amid thin trade.
"It's just incredibly quiet. Crude has probably seen its lows and highs for the day," said Rocky D'Esposito of RJ Futures.
At 1330 EST, February crude was off 29 cents a barrel at $24.79. January heating oil stood 1.52 cents a gallon lower at 71.45 cents, and January gasoline was off 1.44 cents a gallon at 68.75 cents.
Trading was thinned due to the Christmas holiday on Wednesday. NYMEX will close at 1300 EST Christmas Eve on Tuesday and will reopen for regular trading hours Thursday.
"It seems like there is no volume. There is little rhyme or reason for the gasoline move" said a gasoline trader in New York, adding gasoline was initially taken lower by heating oil.

Weather Services Corp said temperatures both Monday and Tuesday are expected to average six to 15 degrees above normal and to average near normal through Friday in the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States.
Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said temperatures should be below normal by late week in the U.S. Northeast, though forecasters had expected a colder average for the week as a whole.

"We came in weak at the open with gas oil down in London," said a heating oil dealer in New York. Gas oil is the European equivalent of heating oil. January gas oil ended $3.50 a tonne weaker at $211.50 on London's IPE.
Heating oil supply was deemed ample as Colonial Pipeline continued to ration space on its line due to high demand by refiners to ship distillate, particulary heating oil, to New York.
Moreover, about 180,000 tonnes of Russian gas oil is due in the United States this week.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
